qc.label_under_test: ' own' after a possessive (its own, their own): something belonging to and separate for that owner

neighbours.label: a small word before a noun (own, a, their, simple) in writing about helping people learn, grow or heal; the same slot in other topics stays quiet
fire: Therapy gives clients a safe space to find their own voice again.
Good teachers help each student discover their own pace of learning.
Recovery starts with a simple step: admitting you need support.
Mentors encourage young people to set their own goals and grow from them.
Journaling is a simple tool that helps many people heal after loss.
The workshop teaches adults to take ownership of their own growth.
Every child deserves a chance to learn at their own speed.
Counselors help grieving families build a new routine together.
quiet: The mechanic fixed the car using his own wrench set.
The factory ships its products at a steady pace each month.
The recipe starts with a simple step: preheat the oven.
The committee set their own budget for the bridge repairs.
A hammer is a simple tool found in most garages.
The company took ownership of the new warehouse downtown.
Every train leaves the station at its own scheduled time.
The city built a new parking garage near the stadium.

predictions: Expect topic to carry it: most fire sentences above 0.2, near misses mostly under 0.15; risk that 'a' or 'simple' fire weaker than 'own'.
